A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same weight-imprinting research and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.2. Relocated and renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments, component comparisons, few-shot evaluations, and neural-collapse measurements in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original classification and neural-collapse experiments, with revised numerical results in the main text and appendix tables.

M1.justification: The generation–normalization–aggregation framework and proposed k-means imprinting with L2 normalization and max aggregation are unchanged. The added NC1 preprocessing disclosure does not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, and remapped ImageNet tasks, including the same few-shot scenarios. Figure 16's expanded displayed range is already covered by Figure 10 in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Qi et al., Hosoda et al., and Janson et al.; Janson's citation is renumbered. The generator, normalization, and aggregation comparator sets also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 revises the reported experiment total from approximately 350,000 to 150,000. Tables 2 and 7 replace the reported k-fps configuration at k=2 with k=20 and k=5, respectively. These reported setting revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing generator ablations are revised through the replacement k-fps configurations in Tables 2 and 7 and updated sensitivity curves in Figure 6. The normalization, aggregation, few-shot, and neural-collapse analyses remain, without a new analysis question or robustness suite.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed medians by default, five-seed averages for few-shot experiments, ten ImageNet remappings, 95% confidence intervals, and critical-difference comparisons using p<0.05. Updated ranks and plotted intervals do not change these reporting practices.

E6.justification: Several accuracies and ranks change while the main findings remain stable. Table 1 changes Hosoda from 82.15% to 80.71% and Ours from 91.47% to 91.48%; Table 2 changes k-means from 91.95% to 91.44%; Table 4 changes the none/none row from 88.36% to 87.76%. Appendix Tables 7–9 also contain updates. The replacement k-fps results use different k values and are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Equation (1), the NC1 definition, and the distance/inner-product argument connecting max aggregation with 1-nn are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation appears.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a unifying imprinting framework, advantages from k-means proxies and normalization, and a connection between neural collapse and imprinting success. The up-to-4% improvement claim is retained. Code availability was already stated in v1.

C2.justification: The interpretations of normalization, proxy count, and neural collapse remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations, and Appendix A.2 retains the model-size/training-regime hypotheses and explanation of Transformer accuracy dips.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly documents L2 normalization of embeddings before computing NC1, improving preprocessing disclosure without establishing that the procedure changed. The abstract repeats the repository link already supplied in v1; it does not establish newly available code.

R1.justification: The cited research and positioning arguments are retained. The additional numbered CIFAR-10 reference replaces an existing footnote citation, while other reference-number changes reflect reordered citations.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and affiliation corrections, repeats the code-release statement in the abstract, and updates cross-references. The section sequence and substantive exposition remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 and its critical-difference chart move earlier, with Figure 4 becoming Figure 2. Plots receive revised typography, colors, spacing, and axes; Figure 16 changes from a linear 10–200 view to a logarithmic 10–400 view. All nine tables and seventeen figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility by documenting NC1 preprocessing and resolves inconsistencies between main-text and appendix results, notably Table 1's Hosoda score and Table 4's none/none row relative to Table 8. Revised plots also reduce label overlap. These are limited quality gains; the unexplained experiment-total and numerical revisions do not establish stronger empirical validation.
